# Quorum - submission README

Four AIs argue each tokenized-stock trade; a Judge rules and keeps the case against.

Live: https://quorum-ten-mauve.vercel.app/app  ·  Repo: https://github.com/dmustapha/quorum

## Problem

"AI trading" demos usually show one model emitting a confident answer with no counter-argument and no honest track record. A trader gets the call but never the strongest reason it is wrong, and never a calibrated hit-rate. They cannot operate on that.

## What we built

Quorum is a research console a trader operates. Pick a scheduled catalyst on a tokenized U.S. stock (a Bitget rToken), press Run live, and a four-role panel runs on 0G decentralized compute: Bull (case for), Bear (case against), Risk (the stop), then a Judge that issues the single order-triggering decision. The debate streams in over about 20 seconds; the losing side is preserved on every verdict, in plain language. A fresh live ruling wears a visibly lesser "LIVE - unstudied" state, never the validated verdict seal.

## Our integration

- **Bitget Agent Hub SDK** (`@bitget-ai/bitget-agent-sdk` 3.3.1) is the single order call-site: LONG routes to a real spot buy, SHORT on a spot-only rToken degrades to an honest advisory signal (no fabricated fill). See [sponsor-tracks.md](./sponsor-tracks.md).
- **Bitget Spot Market API** supplies the point-in-time price context and the committed candle series.
- **0G Compute** (`deepseek-v4-pro`) is the reasoning engine; the whole debate is its live output, proven end to end on production.

## What makes this different

The honesty is the product, enforced in code, not prose:
- **Test the judging.** A conviction-gate slider re-derives the decision in pure code from the stored raw Judge output - drag it, the call flips instantly, with a flip-point marker. It is arithmetic on a stored number and the UI says so.
- **Leak-safe scoreboard.** The calibration curve ("when the panel says 70, how often was it right?") aggregates only out-of-sample study rows. A live console run is recorded to history but can never enter the aggregate - a data gate, not a convention.
- **Every stat carries its n.** Below the significance threshold the numbers render greyed as "directional illustration, not significance-tested." Empty calibration buckets read "no data," never a fabricated 0%.
- **Pre-registration guard.** The pinned point (bar 0.6, horizon 3d) is fixed; slide off it and any out-of-sample claim locks into an explicit exploratory state.

## Verify in 60s

The honesty invariants and the leak-safe scoreboard re-derive deterministically from committed evidence - you do not have to trust the screenshots:

```
git clone https://github.com/dmustapha/quorum && cd quorum
npm install && npm test
```

Expected: `Test Files 24 passed (24) · Tests 104 passed (104)`. These include the leak-safe gate (a live/in-sample row can never enter the scoreboard), the calibration-bucket null-not-zero rule, and the significance render-gate. Then open https://quorum-ten-mauve.vercel.app/app and run a live panel to see the engine itself.

## Try it

1. Open https://quorum-ten-mauve.vercel.app/app, pick a catalyst, press **Run live** - watch Bull/Bear/Risk/Judge stream in.
2. Open the ruling, drag the conviction slider - the call flips NO_TRADE / SHORT / LONG instantly.
3. Open https://quorum-ten-mauve.vercel.app/scoreboard - the calibration curve, every stat n-gated and leak-safe.
